basis: Profound neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; aortic aneurysm in 2/5 supports cardiovascular involvement. Feeding difficulty and incontinence do not establish separate organ damage.
Progressive vitiligo, intellectual disability and urethral duplication define the syndrome; urethra belongs to renal. An autoimmune mechanism is not established for this syndromic form.
Purine metabolic disorder; HPO reports ataxia/hearing loss 80-99% and renal insufficiency 30-79%. Neurologic features vary by subtype; aortic abnormalities omitted at cap.
Frontonasal dysplasia, eye malformations and ear defects define syndrome; encephalocele occurs in 30-79%. VSD and cleft lip also reported in 30-79%, omitted at cap.
Dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causes muscular dystrophy; borderline intellectual disability in 2/2 supports neurologic involvement.
Congenital duplication directly affects the colon.
Defined by postoperative cardiac ventricular dysfunction; its frequency among surgical patients does not change the affected organ.
Pituitary adenoma directly occupies an endocrine gland; hormone excess remains within the endocrine axis.
Oral, digital and ocular anomalies define syndrome; severe intellectual disability is an additional defining feature supporting neurologic involvement.
Lymphoid malignancy arising in a paranasal sinus; sinuses belong to pulmonary. Lymphoma supports haematologic and infectious_immune axes.
Localized dermal amyloid deposition produces chronic pruritic hyperkeratotic papules; systemic organ involvement is not part of this disease.
Malignant hematopoietic histiocytic neoplasm; no specific extranodal organ has established involvement in at least 30%. This is not a lymphoma.
Defined as an autoimmune nervous-system syndrome associated with streptococcal infection, with tics, chorea and developmental regression.
Developmental hypoplasia of the cervical odontoid process; neurologic injury is a possible complication without evidence of frequency reaching 30%.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, with possible vestibular areflexia; both affect the ear axis.
Parkinsonian neurodegeneration defines disease; dysphagia, constipation, diplopia and bladder symptoms do not establish direct damage to additional organs.
Carcinoma originates in the penis, a reproductive organ outside the axes. HPV association does not make the carcinoma an infectious disease.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by cholestasis and renal aminoaciduria/Fanconi dysfunction; hearing impairment is reported in 80-99%.
Umbrella disorder of phosphate homeostasis; no additional organ damage is established across hypophosphatemic and hyperphosphatemic conditions.
Embryonal carcinoma located in the central nervous system.
Sarcoma originates in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; stromal or muscle differentiation does not establish locomotor-system disease.
Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, pigmentary changes and optic disc pallor; retinal vessel attenuation remains within the ocular disease.
Neuroendocrine carcinoma classified under malignant endocrine neoplasm. Thymic epithelial origin alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Gonadotropin-independent sex-hormone excess causes premature puberty; this is an endocrine disorder.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder defined by auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy, both present in 8/8; auditory and optic nerves map to ear and eye here.
